biography.plain_text: Bodo Buschmann built Brabus into an international business specialising in powerful, individually finished Mercedes-Benz cars. The son of a Mercedes dealer, he drew on experience in the family business and began in a workshop behind his parents' dealership. He founded Brabus in Bottrop and led its expansion until his death in 2018.

long_biography.plain_text:
Through the German tuning association VDAT, which he co-founded and chaired, Bodo Buschmann worked to give vehicle modification a stronger professional standing. The association promoted the quality and safety of tuning products, reflecting an approach in which engineering standards mattered alongside performance. His work at Brabus extended from individual customer commissions to partnerships with major manufacturers.

The smart-Brabus joint venture brought the company's modifications into Smart's official model range, an important commercial endorsement from the wider Daimler group. Buschmann pursued a different kind of craftsmanship through Brabus Classic, established in 2013. The division restored older Mercedes-Benz vehicles, applying the company's workshop expertise to preserving cars as well as increasing their performance.

Buschmann pursued a different kind of craftsmanship through Brabus Classic, established in 2013. The division restored older Mercedes-Benz vehicles, applying the company's workshop expertise to preserving cars as well as increasing their performance.
